message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $935 cash and am on SHORT_LINE after paying $50 rent to p4. I own four properties across three monopolies: light blue, pink, and orange. p2 has READING_RAILROAD, NEW_YORK_AVENUE, INDIANA_AVENUE, and MARVIN_GARDENS with no monopoly.

p3 has $320 and owns the brown monopoly with hotels, plus ELECTRIC_COMPANY and BOARDWALK. p4 has $436 and holds ORIENTAL, CONNECTICUT, KENTUCKY, PENNSYLVANIA_RR, and PARK_PLACE.

Green and yellow are split between p2, p4, and the bank. Virginia Avenue is the only remaining unowned property needed to complete the pink monopoly. I will not sell Vermont or the orange properties.

I cannot trade for Virginia because it is bank-owned. I am considering trading p2's New York Avenue to complete the orange monopoly, but they previously rejected a $420 offer for both of my orange properties. I have enough cash to cover the $200 purchase price.

Trading p2's New York Avenue would require overpaying, leaving me unable to build and vulnerable to p3's brown hotels. I cannot trade Vermont for another player because that would complete their light blue set. Trades with p3 or p4 are also unhelpful.

I cannot trade for New York Avenue at a price that still allows me to build. Even paying $400 would leave only $535, which covers five houses but not a full set of three on each orange property. The resulting uneven threat is too risky against p3's Baltic hotel. Indiana and Marvin Gardens are also unhelpful.

No trade offers remain that would not complete another player's monopoly or drain my cash. I will end the turn.
